sections.h2: Which ways of selling fit a Richardson, TX owner?
sections.html:
Owners here choose between a market listing, a sale without an agent, and a direct as-is purchase. Listing rewards a house in strong condition. The as-is option fits someone who wants no repairs, no showings and no long wait.

The city sits in two counties, Dallas and Collin, and that split shapes everything from tax bills to school boundaries. Before you pick a route, work out which county holds your address, which school district serves it, and what you owe on the loan. Those three facts set your floor and your timeline.

  • Listing: broad exposure, then inspection requests and lender timelines.
  • Private sale: no commission, but you handle contract and buyer screening.
  • As-is purchase: no repair list, and you negotiate the closing date.

sections.h2: Where does a Richardson owner pay the county tax bill?
sections.html:
The city's own property tax page tells residents to pay at the county office that covers the address, and it prints contact details for both counties.

Dallas Central Appraisal District appraises for 61 local governing bodies in its county, and its site reported that the Dallas County review board had received over 250,000 protests for 2026, with hearings expected to run into September. Collin CAD handles the Collin side and posts a taxing-entities page with adopted rates. If you plan to contest a value, ask the appraiser for an informal review before the hearing date.

sections.h2: What is Richardson's Home Improvement Incentive Program?
sections.html:
It is a city program that pays homeowners who spend heavily on a single-family remodel. The payment equals ten times the increase in city taxes that results from the higher appraised value.

  • The project must cost at least $20,000 and finish within 24 months of approval.
  • You apply to Community Services before any construction starts and agree to inspections.
  • The appraisal district's certified value decides the tax increase.
  • Owners delinquent on taxes or fees are not eligible.

The city pays on April 1 of the first full calendar year after the work is done, under an economic development agreement. Community Services, at the Temporary City Hall Annex on Campbell Creek Blvd, can be reached at 972-744-4166. The city notes that the payment may count as taxable income. A remodel will not repay you before a sale, but an owner who stays may benefit.

sections.h2: Which schools, colleges and transit routes serve Richardson?
sections.html:
Richardson ISD covers 46 square miles in Dallas County, parts of Richardson, Dallas and Garland, with more than 36,000 students and 50 campuses: 37 elementary schools, eight junior highs, four high schools and one alternative school. Plano ISD takes in northern parts of Richardson on the Collin County side across about 100 square miles.

Colleges nearby include the University of Texas at Dallas, which opened in 1969, Dallas College Richland Campus and Collin College. The city also lists West Coast University and Galen College of Nursing campuses.

For getting around, the city's page describes DART rail and bus, Trinity Railway Express and NTTA tollways. It also lists hike and bike trails and a transportation and mobility department. Buyers who commute by rail will want to know the walking distance to a station, so measure it before you list.

sections.h2: What city services and permits matter before a Richardson sale?
sections.html:
The city's site lists code enforcement, residential building inspection with online permits, floodplain information, a 24/7 response center, trash and brush pickup, and permits for garage sales and alarms. Each can matter when a buyer's inspector asks questions.

  • Confirm permits for any addition or remodel through building inspection.
  • Check the floodplain information page for your address.
  • Pay or close out water service through the water customer service page.
  • Ask about brush and bulky item collection before you clear out a house.

Richardson also keeps a winter water conservation plan, under which residents may water at any time on their designated watering days. The city is building a new city hall and renovating its library as part of bond projects, work that the city's municipal campus pages describe. For a seller, the takeaway is simple: Richardson invests in public buildings, and it expects homes to meet its codes.

sections.h2: What does living in Richardson offer a buyer?
sections.html:
Richardson sells itself on culture and public amenities, which you can point to in a listing. The city site lists the Eisemann Center, a library in a newly renovated building on Arapaho, Sherrill Park Golf Course, a senior center, a tennis center, a gymnastics center and recreation centers.

  • Events such as the Cottonwood Art Festival and the Wildflower Festival.
  • A city Christmas parade, which the home page listed as its 54th edition.
  • Hike and bike trails and public parks.
  • Neighborhood and homeowner association contacts on the city's site.

The city also publishes Richardson Today, a week-in-review email and a MyRichardson app for reporting issues. A buyer who reads these will see a city that communicates often, which can ease concerns about moving. Your listing can mention the nearest park, trail or rail station by name. Specific details beat general praise, and they give a buyer something to check on a drive-by visit.

sections.h2: How are property taxes and exemptions handled at a Richardson closing?
sections.html:
The year's tax lien attached on January 1, so the title company splits the bill between seller and buyer at closing. Bills go out around October 1, and January 31 is the usual cutoff.

From February 1, penalty and interest build, and by July the penalty reaches 12 percent. Installment plans exist for homeowners who are over 65 or disabled. Every school district must give a $140,000 homestead exemption. Disabled veterans get an exemption tied to their rating, and a 100 percent rating exempts the whole homestead. Appraised value on a homestead is capped at a 10 percent yearly increase.

Ask the appraisal district which exemptions sit on your account, since a buyer may need to apply for their own.

sections.h2: What if a Richardson owner has a foreclosure or an inherited house?
sections.html:
A lender that holds a defaulted Texas loan can sell without going to court. The borrower has 20 days after the default letter to catch up, and the sale notice must go out three weeks or more before a first-Tuesday auction.

For an inherited house, the right path depends on the estate. A will can be offered for probate during the four years after death. Estates worth $75,000 or less, not counting the homestead, can use a small estate affidavit that a judge approves. An affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement, and buyers need not accept it. If the owner signed a beneficiary deed of that kind, the heir records proof of death before selling.

Recording is done by the clerk of whichever county covers the parcel, and the state clerk manual sets the per-page recording charge and the other records fees.

faqs.q: Do I pay Richardson property tax to the city?
faqs.a: The city's page says taxes are paid at the county tax office where the property is located, so use the Dallas or Collin County office for your address.

faqs.q: Is Richardson in Dallas County or Collin County?
faqs.a: Both. The city's tax page lists an office for each county.

faqs.q: How big must a project be for the Home Improvement Incentive Program?
faqs.a: At least $20,000, completed within 24 months of approval, with an application filed before construction starts.
Richardson ISD and Plano ISD. RISD spans 46 square miles in Dallas County, and Plano ISD takes in northern parts of the city.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1 for most bills left unpaid after January 31, when penalty and interest begin.
